signals.title: SEK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 strength scorecard confirms SEK as the week's strongest performer with a 1W average gain of +0.941% across two pairs, while EUR lags the complex at -0.471% across nine pairs, establishing a 1.412% bilateral spread. SEK's outperformance runs directly against a nominal policy rate deficit, as the ECB holds at 2.65% versus the Riksbank at 1.75%, leaving EUR with a +90bp nominal carry advantage. However, Swedish inflation expectations of 0.70% yield a real policy rate of +1.05%, significantly more restrictive than the ECB's real rate of +0.30%. This real-yield insulation supports the krona against broad European softness despite domestic Swedish economic surprise readings lagging at -17.0 ESI. Technically, EUR/USD trades at 1.1230, pinned below its descending SMA20 (1.1384), SMA50 (1.1513), and SMA200 (1.1602), confirming persistent EUR weakness across crosses. Trade bias: Bearish EUR against Nordic currencies; structural EUR underperformance dominates despite nominal carry deficits. Catalyst: ECB Schnabel speech today at 13:30 UTC. Risk: A rebound in EUR sentiment compressing the G10 bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Downside Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 158.22, positioned above its SMA20 (157.04) and SMA50 (157.65) while testing resistance just below its SMA200 at 158.51. The structural backdrop remains anchored by a +265bp overnight OIS spread favoring the dollar, reflecting Fed SOFR at 3.88% against BoJ TONA at 1.23%. While speculative CFTC positioning shows JPY leveraged funds net short -16,809 contracts at the 96th percentile of its 52-week range (z = +1.83), the options market displays acute divergence. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal sits at -1.82, showing strong put skew and heavy institutional demand for downside JPY hedges even as IV (8.0%) trades 1.9 points below realized 30-day volatility (9.9%). With VIX contained at 15.4, safe-haven unwinds remain dormant, but the heavy options put skew flags institutional caution on topside momentum as 160.00 watch levels loom. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY on carry dips; topside pace constrained by downside options hedging. Catalyst: US Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation expectations at 14:00 UTC. Risk: A breach above 160.00 prompting verbal or direct Ministry of Finance intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Spec Shorts + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1230, remaining deeply compressed below its descending moving average cluster of SMA20 at 1.1384, SMA50 at 1.1513, and SMA200 at 1.1602. Institutional positioning data shows EUR leveraged funds expanded net short exposure by -23,640 contracts WoW to -82,445 contracts, sitting at the 6th percentile of its 52-week range (z = -1.65). Macro policy differentials reinforce the pressure, as Fed SOFR at 3.88% versus €STR at 2.44% provides an authoritative +144bp OIS carry advantage to the US dollar. Concurrently, 1M EUR/USD implied volatility trades at 6.7% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.3%, generating an elevated volatility risk premium of +2.4% that reflects persistent downside hedging demand. A BEER fair value model reading of z = -1.59 indicates extended valuation cheapness, but the real-rate advantage of +1.63% on USD versus +0.30% on EUR continues to dictate trend direction. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry spreads and short momentum outweigh technical oversold conditions. Catalyst: US Michigan 5-year inflation expectations at 14:00 UTC. Risk: A short-covering squeeze above the SMA20 at 1.1384 triggered by softening US inflation survey data.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Macro Rates Divergence + Retail Positioning Imbalance
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.4216, trading firmly above its SMA20 (1.4105), SMA50 (1.3973), and SMA200 (1.3864) in a confirmed bull trend. Institutional monetary policy divergence remains firmly in the dollar's favor, with Fed SOFR at 3.88% versus BoC CORRA at 2.29%, delivering a +159bp overnight carry premium to the greenback. Rates momentum reinforces the setup, with US 5Y yields gaining +46bp over the past 20 sessions (FRED, as of Oct 06) led almost entirely by real yields (+49bp). CFTC leveraged funds reflect this institutional alignment with CAD net short at -72,519 contracts following a -23,396 WoW reduction. Conversely, retail sentiment shows an extreme 93% short positioning on USD/CAD, establishing a pronounced retail-versus-institutional divergence. The confluence of widening rate differentials and one-sided retail fading supports ongoing spot stability above moving average support. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; structural carry advantage and retail short crowding support upward momentum. Catalyst: Canada employment report at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Significant upside surprise in Canadian employment figures reviving BoC hike expectations and narrowing the 2Y yield gap.
